name: Applicant Real Ticket · the audit check (draft)
description: The check itself. 16 deterministic gates plus 3 verifier rules over one month of applicant flight-ticket spend. Token supplied per run in the request payload; holds no ERP credential. Draft - never published, never scheduled.

parameters.notes:
ERP-COMPLIANCE: no-breaker-because this node reads a batch of ONE. Get Independent Count makes a single call, so consecutive_failures (needs 5), degraded_rate (needs 20 samples) and latency (needs an earlier batch of the same key) are all unreachable by construction - a breaker here could only ever log. What stops the run instead is this node itself: it throws by name on an expired token, INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS, a SecurityException, a missing totalElements and a zero count, and nothing downstream fires until it returns. The fan-outs that CAN be judged are judged: Judge Population Pages, Judge Detail Batch, Judge Tickets Batch, Judge Reversals Batch.

ERP-COMPLIANCE: empty-exit-ok - the sole `return out` is a list of Math.ceil(total/40) page items, and every path that could make that list empty throws by name first: a non-200 (expired token / INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS / SecurityException / anything else), a non-finite totalElements, and `!(total > 0)`. So total >= 1 and out.length >= 1 by construction. Do NOT give this node alwaysOutputData: it is a loud gate, and an injected empty item would turn "ERP denied the population surface" into a green run that scored nothing. Its throws reach Capture Failure -> Release Lease (error).

parameters.notes: ERP-COMPLIANCE: empty-exit-ok - `if (out.length === 0) return [{ json: { txn_id: null, needed: false } }];` runs before the final `return out`, so the final return is only reached with out.length > 0. That sentinel is the whole point of it: Needs Detail? sends it down the false leg to Skip Detail Fallback, so a month in which every row already carries an Applicant ID still reaches Join Detail Paths - and now the release.

parameters.notes: ERP-COMPLIANCE: empty-exit-ok - throws by name (NO APPLICANT COULD BE ATTRIBUTED) when out.length === 0, so `return out` is reached only with >= 1 item. This node must stay loud, and alwaysOutputData would be wrong twice over: its successor is Get Flight Tickets, an ERP call, so an empty sentinel would buy a junk request AND turn a broken identity parse into a green run. The throw reaches Capture Failure -> Release Lease (error).

ERP-COMPLIANCE: empty-exit-ok - `if (out.length === 0) return [{ json: { applicant_id: null, skip: true } }];` precedes the final `return out`. The sentinel carries an empty applicant_id, which is exactly what Any All-Time Lookups? routes down its false leg into Skip All-Time Lookups - and Skip All-Time Lookups is one of the two nodes that now feed Release ERP Lease. So a month that queues no all-time lookup still releases the lease.

options.systemMessage:
You are the verifier for the maids.cc audit "Applicant Real Ticket" (road-map #10, Money Control).

WHAT THIS CHECK IS ABOUT
The company buys real travel tickets for recruitment applicants. A ticket that was
paid for should end one of two ways: the applicant FLEW it, or the money CAME BACK.
A ticket that did neither is money out for something that never happened. The
numbers already establish which tickets ended that way. Only the written record
says whether anybody DECIDED that outcome. Deciding that, and nothing wider, is
your entire job.

YOU ARE NOT ASKED TO DO ARITHMETIC. Every amount, route, status, outcome and
refund search has already been computed and is given to you as fact. Never
recompute an amount, never dispute a figure, and never decide whether a refund
exists in ERP - that search has already run.

CRITICAL VOCABULARY WARNING
On a REAL ticket, outcome "Used" is the HAPPY PATH - the money did exactly what it
was spent for. Never treat a flown ticket as suspicious. On the sibling Dummy
Tickets check "Used" means the opposite; never carry that reading over here.

THE FOUR VERDICTS - return one, EXACTLY as written, never paraphrased:
  "clean - explained"                          the record states a DECISION that makes this outcome expected
  "clean - rebooking justified"                (V2 only) the second booking replaced the first
  "finding - unexplained"                      nothing in the record accounts for the money
  "pending - evidence claimed, not verified"   the record CLAIMS a refund happened outside ERP

TEN HARD STOPS. Each one is a "Never" line from the audit's own policy pages.

 1. Never treat a NAMED REASON as an explanation on its own. refundReason "Other"
    appears on 12 of 120 rows and explains nothing. A label is a pointer to
    evidence, not evidence. Quote the sentence that accounts for the money.

 2. Never accept refundReason ALONE as proof a refund happened. It records why a
    refund was REQUESTED, not that money arrived. Both Lost and Refunded tickets
    can carry one.

 3. Never treat a BLANK record as clean. Absence of an explanation is not an
    explanation. refundReason is empty on 74 of 120 rows, so silence is the common
    case and it is exactly what this check exists to surface.

 4. Never clear more than the ONE TICKET in front of you. Your clean is scoped to
    this ticket. The applicant's case verdict is re-aggregated afterwards as the
    worst of her remaining tickets. One explained loss must never close a second
    unexplained one - applicant 1169535 carries exactly that pair.

 5. Never treat the TICKET COUNT as the question. Multiple real tickets on one
    applicant is normal: visa timing slips, applicants miss flights, airlines are
    switched, and domestic feeder legs are booked separately from the international
    one. The question is whether money was spent twice for ONE journey, or spent
    once and lost.

 6. Never conclude a duplicate when a refund may simply be LATE. If the field
    "ALL-TIME SEARCH PROVABLY COMPLETE" reads no, the honest answer is
    "pending - evidence claimed, not verified", never a finding.

 7. Never accept a claim that the refund was handled OUTSIDE ERP as proof. It
    downgrades to "pending - evidence claimed, not verified" and names who must
    produce the receipt. It never clears the amount.

 8. Never invent the reconciliation. An empty transaction history is evidence only
    when the all-time search ran AND was provably complete. A failed or truncated
    call is not an absence.

 9. Never let a low-confidence clearance stand as a clearance. If you are not
    confident, return "finding - unexplained" or the pending verdict instead.

10. Never quote a sentence you did not find in the evidence given to you. The quote
    must be copied character for character. If there is no such sentence, the quote
    is the empty string and the verdict is not a clearance.

WHAT A REAL EXPLANATION LOOKS LIKE
A manager-approved abandonment IS a business decision and clears the ticket -
"case dropped approved by managers" is a real example from this data. So are ERP's
own "Applicant was caught by airport staff", "Applicant stopped answering" and
"Applicant was not allowed to baord" - that misspelling is ERP's own, do not
correct it and do not treat it as invalidating the reason. A replacement stated
outright - "MISSED HER PREV FLIGHT", "To be cancelled and replaced two weeks
before her flight" - clears a V2 pair. In every case the money is still recorded:
explaining a loss never deletes it from the total.

The notes you are given have had applicant names and passport numbers removed at
source. Never ask for them, never speculate about identity, and never include a
person's name in your output.

const src = $input.first().json;
const p = src.params;
const now = new Date().toISOString();
const out = [];
for (const c of src.cases) {
  out.push({ json: {
    run_id: p.run_id,
    case_key: 'art:' + p.window_from + ':' + c.applicant_id,
    applicant_id: String(c.applicant_id === null ? '' : c.applicant_id),
    window_from: p.window_from, window_to: p.window_to,
    state: c.case_verdict === 'red' ? 'finding' : (c.case_verdict === 'clean' ? 'clean' : (c.case_verdict === 'verifier' ? 'review' : 'pending')),
    verdict: c.case_verdict === 'red' ? 'Ticket lost - money not recovered'
      : c.case_verdict === 'clean' ? 'Flown / Refunded / One journey in legs'
      : c.case_verdict === 'verifier' ? 'Rebooking to confirm / Loss to explain'
      : 'Flight not yet due / Amount unknown / Nothing settled it',
    reason_code: String(c.case_reason || ''),
    reason_text: '',
    exposure_aed: Number(c.exposure_aed) || 0,
    explained_aed: Number(c.explained_aed) || 0,
    unrecovered_aed: Number(c.unrecovered_aed) || 0,
    losses_total: Number(c.losses_total) || 0,
    losses_explained: Number(c.losses_explained) || 0,
    losses_unaccounted: Number(c.losses_unaccounted) || 0,
    exposure_is_complete: c.exposure_is_complete === true,
    unpriced_reds: Number(c.unpriced_reds) || 0,
    count_in_window: c.count_in_window === null ? 0 : Number(c.count_in_window),
    duplicate_gate: (c.duplicate_question && c.duplicate_question.gate) ? String(c.duplicate_question.gate) : '',
    duplicate_answer: c.duplicate_question ? String(c.duplicate_question.answer) : '',
    tickets_real: Number(c.tickets_real) || 0,
    tickets_moneyless: Number(c.tickets_moneyless) || 0,
    red_ticket_ids: c.tickets.filter(function (t) { return t.loss === true; }).map(function (t) { return t.id; }).join(','),
    red_ticket_routes: c.tickets.filter(function (t) { return t.loss === true; }).map(function (t) { return t.route; }).join(','),
    red_charged_in_window: c.red_charged_in_window === true,
    lost_outcome_count: c.tickets.filter(function (t) { return t.reason === 'lost'; }).length,
    refund_failed_count: c.tickets.filter(function (t) { return t.reason === 'refund_failed'; }).length,
    all_time_refund_searched: c.all_time_refund_searched === true,
    all_time_refund_complete: c.all_time_refund_complete === true,
    txn_ids_in_window: (c.txn_ids_in_window || []).join(','),
    ex_refs: (c.ex_refs || []).join(','),
    netted_ex_refs: (c.netted_ex_refs || []).join(','),
    profile_reachable: Number(c.profile_reachable) || 0,
    txn_type_disagrees: c.txn_type_disagrees === true,
    ticket_type_absent: c.ticket_type_absent === true,
    non_aed_present: c.non_aed_present === true,
    unrecognised_states: c.tickets.filter(function (t) { return t.unrecognised; }).map(function (t) { return t.status + '/' + t.outcome; }).join(','),
    ticketing_note_redacted: (c.notes_redacted || []).join(' || ').slice(0, 4000),
    first_seen: now, times_reported: 1, scored_at: now,
    decided_by: c.tickets.some(function (t) { return t.decided_by === 'model'; }) ? 'model' : 'deterministic',
    verifier_verdict: '', verifier_quote: '',
    // Ruled 2026-08-26 (D12). A terminal pending exists BECAUSE a person must
    // look: gate 16 no_gate_matched, gate 13 flight not yet due, gate 12 amount
    // unknown, gate 30 erp_unreachable. Shipping those with the flag down parked
    // 30 cases in a queue nobody was told to open. 'excluded' and 'clean' still
    // raise no hand.
    needs_human: c.case_verdict === 'red' || c.case_verdict === 'verifier' || c.case_verdict === 'pending'
  } });
}
return out;

// Counts, flags and totals ONLY. No per-applicant amount reaches this row.
const src = $('Adjudicate').first().json;
const p = src.params;
const pop = src.population || {};
const s = src.summary || {};
return [{ json: {
  run_id: p.run_id, check_id: p.check_id, check_name: p.check_name,
  window_from: p.window_from, window_to: p.window_to, trigger: p.trigger,
  started_at: p.started_at, completed_at: new Date().toISOString(),
  acting_user: String((p.erp_auth && p.erp_auth.acting_user) ? p.erp_auth.acting_user : ''),
  txns_seen: Number(pop.txns_seen) || 0, txns_pages: Number(pop.pages_fetched) || 0,
  total_elements_reported: Number(pop.total_elements_reported) || 0,
  population_complete: pop.population_complete === true,
  applicant_rows: Number(pop.applicant_scope_rows) || 0,
  maid_rows_excluded: Number(pop.maid_rows_excluded) || 0,

  applicants_seen: Number(pop.applicants_seen) || 0,
  applicants_unreachable: Number(pop.applicants_unreachable) || 0,
  ticket_reads: Number(pop.ticket_reads) || 0,
  alltime_reads: Number(pop.alltime_reads) || 0,
  detail_fallback_reads: Number(pop.detail_fallback_reads) || 0,
  erp_calls_made: Number(s.erp_calls_made) || 0,
  cases_scored: Number(s.cases_scored) || 0,
  red: Number(s.red) || 0, green: Number(s.green) || 0, pending: Number(s.pending) || 0, review: Number(s.review) || 0,
  exposure_total_aed: Number(s.exposure_total_aed) || 0,
  explained_total_aed: Number(s.explained_total_aed) || 0,
  unrecovered_total_aed: Number(s.unrecovered_total_aed) || 0,
  exposure_in_window_aed: Number(s.exposure_in_window_aed) || 0,
  exposure_is_complete: s.exposure_is_complete === true,
  unpriced_reds: Number(s.unpriced_reds) || 0,
  gate14_cleared: Number(s.gate14_cleared) || 0, gate15_routed: Number(s.gate15_routed) || 0,
  catchall_pending: Number(s.catchall_pending) || 0, non_aed_routed: Number(s.non_aed_routed) || 0,
  verifier_down: Number(s.verifier_down) || 0,
  esc_zero_count_contradiction: Number(s.esc_zero_count_contradiction) || 0,
  esc_ticket_type_absent: Number(s.esc_ticket_type_absent) || 0,
  esc_txn_type_disagreement: Number(s.esc_txn_type_disagreement) || 0,
  unimplemented_rules_declared: (src.unimplemented || []).join(' | '),
  spec_deviations: (src.deviations || []).join(' | '),
  blocked_surfaces: '',
  overall: pop.population_complete === true ? (s.exposure_is_complete ? 'complete' : 'complete-with-unpriced-reds') : 'INCOMPLETE',
  notes: 'DRAFT build. Portal delivery not wired - no callback path has been issued for this check.',
  // D16/D9, 2026-08-26. This run is the current one for its window until a later
  // run says otherwise. Mark Prior Runs Superseded, one node upstream, has already

  superseded: false

parameters.content:
## 1 — Intake and token

The ERP bearer and device id arrive in the **request payload, per run**. Nothing is stored in a credential and this flow holds no ERP credential of its own, so every read is logged under the identity of the person who triggered it.

The token is JWT-decoded here: expiry and the device claim are checked before a single ERP call is made. A dead token answers **HTTP 500 with `"Token not valid, {Token is expired}"`**, never a 401 — so it is named as an expired token rather than reported as a server fault.

The window must be a **completed** period. Auditing a month that has not finished cannot say whether it was handled correctly.

## 2 — Population, walked to completion (gate ❶)

`expense.id = 137` only. **Never** filter on `transactionType = 'APPLICANT'` — 5 genuine applicant tickets a month are typed `UNKNOWN` and would vanish silently. The discriminator is the description prefix `Applicant - ` vs `Maid - `; 9.6% of this expense bucket is maid tickets and out of scope.

**`size=40`, never higher.** ERP caps a page at 40 rows while the offset stays `page × size`, so `size=50` never asks for offsets 40–49 and the gap looks like an absence.

The guard aborts the run on an incomplete walk, zero rows, or any foreign expense id. Names and passport numbers are stripped from every description **here, at the boundary**, before anything downstream can see them.

## 3 — Identity and netting (gates ❸, ❺)

The applicant id is parsed from the description (`Applicant ID - (\d+)`, present on 349 of 387 rows). The per-transaction detail call is the **fallback only** — making it unconditionally costs ~349 extra calls a month and breaches the run budget on its own. Identity is **never** resolved by name.

Reversals are netted by `ExNNNNNN` reference **before** anything is counted. 32.6% of this book is negative. The refund fee is retained so a pair never sums to zero — matching is by reference first with a tolerance, never on an exact equal-and-opposite amount.

## 4 — The gates (❷, ❼–⓰)

**First match wins, in `Order` sequence, per ticket.** Gates ⓮ and ⓯ answer only the *duplicate question* at case level — they never overwrite a per-ticket verdict, because ⓮ clears 12 multi-leg journeys a month and 2 of those applicants are carrying real losses.

⓮ tests **arrival == departure**, not destination inequality — two legs of one trip have *different* destinations. The layover is **not** the destination: 60 of 67 layovers are DXB while the real destinations are RUH, KWI, AMM.

On a REAL ticket `Used` is the **happy path** — the exact inverse of its meaning on the sibling Dummy Tickets check. Inverting it would flag a third of the population and clear nothing.

⓫ is the only red, and it does **not** require the ≥2 count: a single lost ticket is a full loss, and the count finds the same money at 5-of-30 where the outcome finds it at 5-of-5.

This node's gate logic is the exact text that passes 5 spec test cases + 15 edge guards offline.

## 5 — The refund is sought without a date filter (gate ❿)

**The window truncates the refund.** A ticket charged inside the window is frequently refunded in a later month, so a windowed read shows a charge with no offsetting reversal and looks like an unrecovered duplicate.

One all-time call per still-unresolved applicant — `description` `like`, **no date filter**. `operation: "contains"` returns **HTTP 500**; `like` returns 200. That was a wrong operator, not a role permission.

An empty history is evidence only when the walk is **provably complete**. A truncated call is not an absence.

## 6 — The verifier gets the residue, never the bulk

Measured load on a complete month: **8 ticket rows / 5 applicants** for V❶ and **7 applicants** for V❷, out of 261 applicants. Most explanations are already structured — `refundReason` states the rebooking outright on 17 of 120 rows — which keeps those deterministic and out of the model's hands entirely.

Every verifier clean is scoped to **one ticket**. `Adjudicate` re-aggregates the case afterwards as the worst of the remaining tickets, so one explained loss can never close a sibling unexplained one.

Notes reaching the model have names and passport numbers already removed at source. A verifier that fails to answer is recorded as `verifier_down` — never as a clean.

## 7 — Delivery. DRAFT — never publish

Per-applicant amounts and ids live in the **Cases** table. That store is "behind the case". The **Runs** row carries counts, flags and totals only — no per-person amount reaches it, and no name or passport number reaches either table.

`delivery.portal` is **false**: no Security Room callback path has been issued for this check, so no reachable node posts anywhere. The placeholder exists so the payload shape is stable, not so something can be fired at it by accident.

Every run declares its three spec deviations and any unimplemented rule in the Runs row, so a quietly absorbed gap cannot look like a clean month.

The error rail writes a `FAILED` run row, so a crashed run is visible rather than absent.

## 8 - Crash path

An Error Trigger writes a `crashed` run row, so a failed run is never a silent absence. The run store distinguishes *nothing found* from *never completed*.

nodes.name: Mark Prior Runs Superseded
nodes.notes: D16/D9. Stamps every EARLIER run of this check for this window as superseded, so a reader summing the Runs table gets one run per window instead of two or three. Runs BEFORE Write Run: at this point every row matching check_id + window_from is a predecessor by construction, so the filter needs only two equals conditions and no not-equals on run_id - a condition no Data Table filter in these flows uses, and one that could not be tested from here. It sits IN the chain rather than on a branch off Adjudicate because addConnection appends, so a branched stamp would execute after Write Run and mark the new row superseded. Matching zero rows is the normal first-run case; alwaysOutputData keeps Build Run Row reachable when it happens, because a Data Table node that matches nothing emits no items. SUPERSEDED MEANS ONLY 'a later run for this window exists' - not that the later run was good. That is the overall column's job.

nodes.name: Run Config
nodes.notes: Shapes the envelope Validate Inputs expects, for both the monthly schedule and a manual re-run. Deliberately emits NO headers key: Validate Inputs guards its shared-secret check with `if (viaHttp)`, which tests `raw.headers`, so a non-HTTP entry skips it by that node's own design rather than by anything being bypassed here.

nodes.name: Run Monthly
nodes.notes: Monthly on the 15th at 06:00 Asia/Dubai. The window itself comes from Validate Inputs' lastMonth() default, so this trigger only decides WHEN, never WHICH month.

nodes.name: Run Manually
nodes.notes: Test entry. Shares Run Config with the schedule so a manual run exercises exactly the scheduled path.
